headline: Bangladesh seeks Hasina's extradition from India, says no passport needed for 'fugitive'
summary: The State Minister for Foreign Affairs stated that Sheikh Hasina, labeled a 'terrorist' and 'fugitive,' would be handed over under the active extradition treaty between Bangladesh and India, negating the need for travel documents.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir announced that Bangladesh seeks the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from India under an active treaty. He explicitly stated that no passport or travel documents would be required for her return.

Kobir made these remarks at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, where he referred to Hasina as a "terrorist" and a "fugitive." He asserted that the process is a legal handover, not a regular visit requiring travel documents.

The State Minister stressed that there is no legal requirement to issue a passport for a fugitive sought under an extradition process. He added that Bangladesh would continue to pursue her return through established legal and diplomatic channels.
caption:
Bangladesh's State Minister for Foreign Affairs has declared that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will be sought for extradition from India, without the need for a passport.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir announced that Bangladesh seeks the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from India under an active treaty. He explicitly stated that no passport or travel documents would be required for her return.

Kobir made these remarks at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, where he referred to Hasina as a "terrorist" and a "fugitive." He asserted that the process is a legal handover, not a regular visit requiring travel documents.

The State Minister stressed that there is no legal requirement to issue a passport for a fugitive sought under an extradition process. He added that Bangladesh would continue to pursue her return through established legal and diplomatic channels.

headline_marked: Two DGFI members [[dismissed and jailed for one year]] after court martial in Mohammadpur extortion case
headline: Two DGFI members dismissed and jailed for one year after court martial in Mohammadpur extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were found guilty of attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur, leading to their dismissal and imprisonment.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each. This follows a court martial after their arrest in an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.

The convicts are identified as Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman. Intelligence sources confirmed on Thursday that the allegations against them were proven during the court martial proceedings.

The incident occurred on October 25 this year, when the two were among six people arrested by police. They were accused of confining motorcycle trader Mohammad Sharif in a flat in Chandrima Model Town, Mohammadpur, and demanding Tk 10 lakh.

Sharif had initially gone to the flat with an Ansar member on October 24, who had offered to help him buy a motorcycle. Four individuals later entered the flat, confined him, and demanded the money, also taking Tk 70,000 he had brought for the purchase.

After being assaulted and threatened, Sharif was allegedly forced into a car around 3:00 am on October 25. He managed to escape at a tea stall near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli when he spotted a police patrol vehicle and informed them.

Police subsequently arrested the six individuals, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car. Following their arrest in the case filed by the businessman, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were handed over to the army for trial under military law.
